Malchishua
mal-kih-SHOO-uh
proper noun
Hebrew Malkishua (H4444), my king is salvation — from melek (H4428), king, and yasha (H3467), to save, to deliver; written Melchishua at 1 Samuel 14:49.

Biblical Definition

Malchishua was a son of King Saul, named with Jonathan, Ishui and Abinadab in the royal genealogy (1Sa 14:49, where the Authorized Version spells it Melchishua; 1Ch 8:33; 9:39). He died with his father and brothers on Mount Gilboa when the Philistines overtook the house of Saul, and Israel's first dynasty ended in a single day on a hillside. Nothing else is told of him — no word, no act, no judgment passed on his character. He is a son who fell with his father. The name is the sharpest thing about him: my king is salvation. Saul named his sons as a believing Israelite named sons, with confessions — Jonathan, the LORD has given; Malchishua, my king is salvation; Eshbaal and Meribbaal, names later prudently altered by the chroniclers. The confession in Malchishua's name is true, and the tragedy is what Saul made of it. The king he had in view was, in the end, himself; and the reign that began with a man head and shoulders above the people ended with the sons of that house dead on Gilboa. Only the King who is Himself the salvation of His people saves those who die with Him.

Origin & Era

A son of King Saul, slain with his father and brothers on Mount Gilboa; his name means my king is salvation.

MALCHISHUA, Hebrew Malkishua, my king is salvation; written Melchishua in 1 Samuel.

A son of Saul the first king of Israel.

Named with Jonathan, Ishui and Abinadab among the sons of Saul.

He fell with his father and his brethren in the battle on mount Gilboa.

From melek, a king, and yasha, to save.

Key Scripture

1Sa 14:49 — "Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchishua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal:"

1Ch 8:33 — "And Ner begat Kish, and Kish begat Saul, and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal."

1Sa 31:2 — "And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchishua, Saul's sons."

1Ch 9:39 — "And Ner begat Kish; and Kish begat Saul; and Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal."

Modern Corruption

Salvation is claimed by association — family, church, heritage; Scripture makes it personal union with the King who saves.

expand to see more

Malchishua carried a true confession in his name, was born into the royal house of Israel, was brother to Jonathan whom Scripture honours, and died on Gilboa under his father's ruin. His case presses the question that every covenant community must keep asking: whether nearness to the things of God is the same as salvation. It is not. They are not all Israel, which are of Israel (Rom 9:6). A man may be the son of a king of Israel, bear a name that says my king is salvation, and be buried under the judgment that fell on his house.

This is not to pronounce on Malchishua's soul, of which Scripture says nothing and about which the dictionary will say nothing. It is to name the false inference — that proximity saves. The Lord Jesus warned that many would say Lord, Lord and be told I never knew you (Mat 7:22-23), and He said it to religious people with impeccable connections. The principle to recover is that the King who is salvation saves persons, one at a time, by uniting them to Himself through faith; and that the most orthodox name in Israel, worn without that union, is a sentence a man does not possess.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Malkishua (H4444), from melek (H4428), king, and yasha (H3467), to save, deliver.

expand to see more

Hebrew melek (H4428) — a king; the LORD is our king; he will save us (Isa 33:22).

Hebrew yasha (H3467) — to save, deliver, give victory; the root of Joshua and of the name Jesus.

Hebrew Malkishua (H4444) — a son of Saul; 1 Samuel 14:49, 31:2, 1 Chronicles 8:33, 9:39.

Hebrew yeshuah (H3444) — salvation, deliverance; the LORD is my strength and song, and is become my salvation (Exo 15:2).

Greek Iesous (G2424) — Jesus; he shall save his people from their sins (Mat 1:21).

Usage

"“Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchishua”."

"“Saul begat Jonathan, and Malchishua, and Abinadab, and Eshbaal”."

"“My king is salvation” — a true confession borne in the house of Saul."
